text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected on /streaming/generate (p95 > 1s for 10m). Paging on-call. Severity: P2. Affected percent: ~8% requests.

alice (oncall): on it. pinging runtime and prod-eng. assigning triage. will post updates here.

miguel (runtime): seeing a spike in tail latency correlated with preproc CPU on the tokenizer workers. p95 jumped from ~180ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~3.8s. streaming connections are hitting stalled frames.

tara (prod-eng): confirmed. streaming stall rate up ~4x. looks like requests hitting heavy prompt-template expansion + JSON-mode tool schema validation path.

sam (devex): any recent rollouts to prompt templates or evals?

jess (support): we have 3 customers reporting slow / stalled responses via support. low user-visible error rate but heavy timeouts for long-chat streaming.

alice (oncall): quick customer impact assessment: roughly 1200 reqs/min on that route, ~8% affected = ~96 reqs/min degraded. Not full outage but SLO breach. Need mitigation to bring p95 under 500ms.

miguel (runtime): quick mitigations we can try now: 1) temporarily route streaming requests to warmed model variant (lower preproc), 2) increase preproc worker pool for tokenizer service, 3) disable JSON-mode strict validation for streaming route. I can flip (2) and (3) now.

tara (prod-eng): +1 to route fallback. patching routing policy to prefer cached-prefix model variant reduces tokenization overhead. I'll coordinate canary now.

sam (devex): note: disabling JSON-mode will change tool schema behavior for a subset of requests — need to notify support before toggling.

jess (support): ok will send a short note to affected customers: "Temporary degradation mitigations in progress; minimal functional impact expected."

oliver (ml-infra): what about batching? Increasing batch size might reduce cost but increase latency — avoid for streaming. Maybe reduce batching for streaming and increase parallel tokenizers.

kevin (sre): creating an incident channel + runbook link. runbook suggests: check preproc CPU, toggle json-mode, scale tokenizer, route to fallback.

alice (oncall): executing plan: (A) scale tokenizer preproc workers x2, (B) disable JSON-mode validation on /streaming/generate, (C) enable routing fallback to model-variant v2-warm for 30% of traffic.

miguel (runtime): running command to scale preproc pool now:
```
kubectl scale deploy/tokenizer-preproc --replicas=6 -n prod
# current 3 -> 6
```

miguel (runtime): scaling done, CPU usage per pod dropped ~30%. tail latencies improving for preproc.

alice (oncall): toggling json-mode off for streaming route (will set flag in config service).

sam (devex): config patch: `feature.json_mode_validation=false` for route `/streaming/generate` applied via ssm.

sam (devex): note: telemetry shows ~7% of streaming requests used tool-schema branch. disabling reduces preproc time ~120ms median.

kevin (sre): enabling routing fallback canary to 30% -> `traffic_policy:set routing.fallback_variant=v2-warm@30%`

tara (prod-eng): canary live. early signals: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 620ms within 3m for canaryed traffic.

miguel (runtime): overall cluster numbers: p95 now ~720ms, p99 ~1.6s. still above target but trending down. streaming stalls reduced by ~60%.

jess (support): sent customer note: "We've applied mitigations; you may see minor changes to tool validation while we stabilize. We'll follow up with timeline."

alice (oncall): good. Next steps: keep canary for 10m, if stable ramp fallback to 60% then full. Also collect samples for affected traces to root cause.

oliver (ml-infra): capturing flamegraphs and a couple of request traces for p99. Looks like heavy CPU in prompt-template renderer when tool-schema present + deep JSON-mode parsing.

sam (devex): can we capture a sanitized example of the worst-case prompt template? I want to add it to the regression suite.

tara (prod-eng): I'll extract a sample (sanitized) from logs and put in /incidents/1704359999/artifacts.

miguel (runtime): small follow-up: temporary scale gives us headroom but doesn't address root parser inefficiency. proposing: 1) short-term patch to cache rendered templates keyed by user+template-hash, 2) optimize JSON-mode parser to short-circuit on streaming routes.

kevin (sre): agree. create JIRA for both with P0/P1 priority.

alice (oncall): status update at +25m: p95=420ms, p99=980ms, streaming stalls back down to baseline-ish. Can start ramping fallback to 70%.

jess (support): customers updated. no new tickets in last 15m.

miguel (runtime): bumped fallback to 70%. backend metrics show steady p95=360ms now.

alice (oncall): closing active paging window in 30m if stable. Opening post-incident follow-up: owner tara (prod-eng) + miguel (runtime) + sam (devex). Postmortem target: timeline + root cause + follow-up fixes (template cache + parser short-circuit + add perf regression tests).

tara (prod-eng): I'll own the postmortem write-up. expecting ~48h to publish.

miguel (runtime): will put up a branch with caching change for review tomorrow.

sam (devex): will add a regression harness and synthetic tests for JSON-mode streaming paths.

kevin (sre): final notes: runbook worked, mitigation options available. recommend adding an automated alert that flags prompt-template expansion time > 200ms per request to catch earlier.

jess (support): draft of customer postmortem message ready if needed.

alice (oncall): incident status: mitigated, customer impact low-medium, follow-ups assigned. I'm marking incident as monitored — will send final summary when postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3. Incident channel will remain open for follow-ups.

kevin (sre): copying action items -> JIRA: INF-3198 (template-cache), INF-3199 (json-parser-shortcircuit), INF-3200 (alerting).

tara (prod-eng): uploading sanitized sample and perf graphs to the incident doc.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone.

jess (support): closing customer comms loop — will reopen if we see regressions.

miguel (runtime): one more: recommend we add a canary that measures tokenization micro-latencies per model-variant so routing can avoid variants with high preproc cost automatically. I'll add a ticket.

alice (oncall): noted. end of thread.
